prediction: Written 2026-10-07 after the 18 trainings finished (2026-10-06) and before any sampling or scoring. Not recorded before submission (2026-10-03); taken from CLAUDE.md backlog item 8 (D4 aug design). Definitions: G = PCA32 novelty (pixel-standardized PCA fit on 1024 evenly spaced maps of nf_fig2_u128_d2p15_noaug_200k, real-real nearest-other 95th-percentile threshold, as in notebooks/dit_l16_zero_init_generalization_pca95.ipynb) with --orbit d4 (max over 8 D4 elements; own orbit excluded from the real-real threshold). Memorized at N iff G < 0.5 OR the pixel-space centred-cosine nearest-training copy fraction with --orbit d4shift (D4 x all periodic shifts, q95 orbit-excluded train-train threshold) >= 0.5. N_T = smallest grid N not memorized. Baseline N_T from noaug u128 re-scored with the same evaluate_run.py (the 'near 1024' in CLAUDE.md used PCA6697 at a different setup and is not comparable). Prediction: for d4shift and d4equiv, N_T(arm) >= N_T(noaug)/8, and N = 64 is memorized for both. Falsified if either arm is not memorized at N = 64, or N_T(arm) < N_T(noaug)/8. If N_T(noaug) <= 512 the factor-8 part is untestable on this grid (min N = 64). warp is a distortion control only: never counted as generalization; its G is reported only beside its P(k) band ratios and the train-vs-held-out reference.
question: Does training-time D4 augmentation (d4shift) or a D4-equivariant UNet (d4equiv) move the UNet-128 memorization-to-generalization transition to smaller N than the no-aug baseline, when copies are searched over the D4 orbit?
